title: Finite-level affine restriction dictionary for the formal-functions input
statement: Let $Y$ be Noetherian, $J$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaf data, $f:X\to Y$ proper, $F$ coherent, and $U$ affine [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, pqf-def-coherent]. Put $R=\Gamma(Y,U)$, $I=J(U)$, $V=f^{-1}U$, $Z=V$ as an open subscheme, $g=(f|_U):Z\to U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$, $K=(J\mathcal O_X)|_V$ and $P=F|_V$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Let $G$ take global sections of modules on $Z$, restricted to scalars $R$ along $g$, and let $E$ evaluate modules on $Y$ over $U$. Then $g$ is proper, $P$ is coherent, $K$ is the comap along $g$ of the ideal sheaf associated with $I$, and there are isomorphisms $a:E(f_*F)\cong G(P)$ and $b:(P/K^{n+1}P)_n\mathbin\circ G\cong(f_*(F/(J\mathcal O_X)^{n+1}F))_n\mathbin\circ E$ such that $b_n\circ G(\pi_n)\circ a$ equals the original pushforward quotient projection on $U$. This asserts only identifications before taking inverse limits, and no completion or formal-functions conclusion.

proof.text: The restriction square is cartesian and the affine chart is an isomorphism, so g is proper by stability of properness under base change and composition. Restriction preserves coherence by its local definition, or by quasi-coherence and finite type on the locally Noetherian restricted scheme.

On the affine scheme U.toScheme, compare ideals on the top open using Scheme.IdealSheafData.ext_of_isAffine. The formula ideal_comap_of_isOpenImmersion computes the top ideal of J.comap U.ι as J(U) transported by the restriction ring isomorphism; ofIdealTop_ideal computes the top ideal of the spectrum ideal as I.map (ΓSpecIso R).inv.hom. The isoSpec appTop identity identifies these ring transports. Finally comap_comp and the restriction-square equation V.ι ≫ f = (f ∣_ U) ≫ U.ι identify the two comaps on Z. This is the affine ideal correspondence of Tags 01I8 and 01IC specialized to the given chart; no ideal-product assertion is used here.

Pushforward over U evaluates F on f^(-1)U. The restriction top isomorphism identifies these sections with global sections of P. The formula for the affine chart appTop identifies the g-induced R-action, giving a. This uses only the section formula for restriction, not formal functions.

For every exponent, use the proved restrictionQuotientIso and restrictionQuotientIso_pi helpers in TorsionControlledFormalRestriction through import all: restriction preserves ideal products, powers and cokernels, and the cokernel comparison is characterized by its quotient projection. Taking sections gives b_n and its displayed equation. The proved restrictionCompletionIso assembles these maps into b; alternatively cancel each quotient epimorphism to prove the transition squares.

lean.statement: theorem formalFunctions_affine_restriction_dictionary {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y] (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (F : CoherentModules X) (U : Y.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) : let R := Γ(Y, U) let I := J.ideal ⟨U, hU⟩ let V := f ⁻¹ᵁ U let Z := V.toScheme let g := (f ∣_ U) ≫ hU.isoSpec.hom let K := (J.comap f).comap V.ι let P := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj F.obj let G := RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Z.toRingedSpace ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).inv ≫ g.appTop).hom let H := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F.obj let T := formalCompletionSystem (J.comap f) F.obj ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f let E := SheafOfModules.evaluation Y.ringCatSheaf (op U) IsProper g ∧ RingedSpace.IsCoherent Z.toRingedSpace P ∧ K = (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop (I.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).inv.hom)).comap g ∧ ∃ a : E.obj H ≅ G.obj P, ∃ b : formalCompletionSystem K P ⋙ G ≅ T ⋙ E, ∀ n : ℕ, a.hom ≫ G.map (formalModuleQuotientπ K (n + 1) P) ≫ b.hom.app (op n) = E.map ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).map (formalModuleQuotientπ (J.comap f) (n + 1) F.obj))
